newsitem.title: USA: NYC presale garners $66 mln, falls short of goal.
newsitem.headline: NYC presale garners $66 mln, falls short of goal.

text.p: New York City's bonds drew $66 million of orders from retail buyers as the presale period began, falling short of the over $100 million mark set during the last bond offering, a city official said Friday.
"It was a little bit on the light side, but we didn't get out until midday," said the New York City official, who declined to be named.
"We're going to take full advantage of the fact that we still have a day-and-a-half to go," the city official added, noting the retail presale period does not end until Tuesday at 1300 EDT.
When New York City sold general obligation bonds in early April, individual investors bought $304 million of bonds in the presale period, only about $30 million short of the record set in March 1996.
A top yield of six percent was set in 2016 for the $739 million of bonds that the city plans to bring to market on Wednesday.
